about: Follow-up planner (the harness, layer 1): ledger in, plan out. Every platform's planner must reproduce every case. The iPhone suite runs this file (ios/Bobby/Tests/HarnessGoldenTests.swift); the rules are in ios/Bobby/Sources/V18/Harness/HarnessPlanner.swift and HarnessLedger.swift.

format.case: name, now, timeZone, options (only what differs from `defaults`), events, expectedPlan
format.times: ISO 8601 with an offset: an instant. `timeZone` (IANA) is the calendar the plan is made in.
format.events: Given in file order and written into the ledger one by one: it sorts them by time, upper-cases a symbol, drops an event whose symbol is not one, drops every `appOpen` (a kind the first build kept and nothing read: a port must accept it in a stored ledger and keep none), and ignores what is dated after `now`. Fields: kind (ask, saved, appOpen, sent, opened, returned, picked, thesis), at, symbol, price (ask), step and sector (sent, opened, returned), ref (opened, returned: the `at` of the follow-up answered), origin (ask: `followUp` when Bobby wrote the question: the button of a follow-up, a board row, the question after a read, a chip that asks about an asset; absent when the person asked in their own words), thread (ask: their own second question about the same read), horizon (ask: what the question named; thesis: what they set), horizonHours (saved: 24, 72 or 168).
format.expectedPlan: Earliest first. step, fireAt, symbol; days for an asset (whole local days from the question); sector for a sector; others for a week (how many other assets it holds). A field that is absent is not compared.
format.sectors: The sector of each symbol the cases use (null: none). The 'With the sector' cases need nothing else from the sector table.
format.constants: What the cases rest on besides the options. waitDays: whole days from a question to its first follow-up, by the horizon it named (null: no follow-up about the asset, the week only). saveWaitDays: the same for the review chosen on a save; 24 hours is where the picker starts, says nothing and is not listed. thesisHorizon: how the horizon set on a thesis is written into the ledger. Interest halves every interestHalfLifeDays, except a thesis, which counts whole while its pointer is there.

cases.name: Nothing is planned before any question: opening the app is not one.
One question: the asset the next day at the time they asked, then the week on Monday.
A late question is followed up at nine in the evening.
A night question is followed up at nine in the morning.
The week counts every asset asked about since the Monday before it, and names the latest when each was asked once.
An asset asked about before the Monday before the week is not part of it.
A question on Monday is part of the week that arrives seven days later, whatever the hour.
A question on Sunday: the asset on Monday, and no week (the Monday after is not their week any more).
A paying account with the Monday briefing gets no second week.
A question older than fourteen days is not followed up.
Nothing is ever planned in the past: a day that passed unseen is not sent late.
Events may arrive in any order: the plan reads them in time.
A symbol in lower case is the same asset, and something that is not a symbol is not kept.
What is dated after now has not happened yet.
Follow-ups turned off, the risk notice withdrawn, everything erased: an empty ledger plans nothing.
The phone was not allowed to show notifications: nothing is written as shown, and the days that passed are not made up for.
Permission taken away after one was shown: it was shown, and it counts.
An ignored asset is followed by the week.
After the asset and the week there is nothing, however long they wait.
A tap on the notification changes nothing: no new chain, the same week at the same hour.
An answer does not start the chain again: the week, and that is all.
Both answered, and still nothing more until they ask again.
A read Bobby started is not a question: nothing is planned from it alone.
A read Bobby started does not take the chain from the question before it: same asset, same clock.
A new question of their own takes the chain: that asset, from that moment.
A second question of their own about the same read is a question.
maxPerQuestion is the most one question gets, whatever the chain holds.
maxPerQuestion counts what was already shown for the question.
The chain is data: it may be the week alone.
Three in a row that nobody answered: the rest is dropped.
Inside the two weeks of quiet a new question is not followed up.
Two weeks after the last one a question may be followed up again; the asset kind still rests, the week comes.
A tap does not end the unanswered streak: three tapped and never answered is quiet.
An answer ends the streak, and the week names the asset they answered about.
A kind whose last two showings went unanswered rests; another kind still comes.
A tap does not keep a kind from resting.
An older answer does not keep a kind alive: the last two were ignored, whatever came before.
The hour they answer at is learned from three answers, never from taps; it stays inside 09:00-21:00 and 18 hours after the question.
Never more than four in seven days: with four shown, a new question gets nothing inside them.
Once one of the four has left the seven days, the next question is followed up, at the hour they answer.
A week is not repeated within six days.
The week is never sooner than 18 hours after the question: Monday at nine is ten hours away, and the Monday after is not their week.
With 18 hours to spare the same week comes.
After a change of time zone everything is planned on the local clock of now.
Intraday maps to the next day: a horizon never brings a follow-up sooner than the next day.
An unspecified horizon is the next day.
A question that named the week waits three days.
A question that named the month waits seven days, and by then it has no week.
A question about years gets no follow-up about the asset at all: the week only.
The hour stays the hour of the question inside 09:00-21:00, however long the wait.
The review they chose on the save outranks what the question named: 168 hours waits seven days.
A save at 72 hours waits three days.
A save left at 24 hours says nothing: it does not shorten what the question named.
A save without a horizon is only a save.
A save from before the question belongs to another read.
A thesis they wrote about the asset outranks the save and the question: a thesis of weeks waits seven days.
A thesis of months or years: no follow-up about the asset, the week only.
A thesis with no horizon set leaves the question's horizon in charge.
A thesis about another asset does not time this one, and is not a question about that asset.
A thesis pointer is not forgotten after sixty days: it lasts as long as its thesis.
Once the asset arrived at its horizon, the week.
The horizon is the one of the question the chain belongs to, not of a read Bobby started later.
A later question of their own brings its own horizon.
A thesis makes its asset the one that matters most.
A second question about the same read counts twice; a read Bobby started counts once.
A tap weighs less than an answer: the week names the asset they answered about, not the one they only tapped.
With the sector: the asset, its sector the day after, the week on Monday.
With the sector: an asset that has none skips that step.
With the sector: an ignored asset is followed by its sector, then the week.
With the sector: after the sector, the week.
With the sector: after the three, silence.
With the sector: three answered is still three, and then nothing.
With the sector: a tap changes nothing either.
With the sector: a sector is not repeated within a week.
With the sector: a kind whose last two went unanswered rests, and the sector takes its day.
With the sector: the sector follows the asset by a day when the asset waits for its horizon.
With the sector: a question about years gets neither the asset nor its sector.
With the sector: after a change of time zone a follow-up never lands on the local day one was already shown, nor within 18 hours of it.
A save with a week's review after the asset was shown does not move the week: it stays the Monday after the day the asset was shown.
A thesis of weeks written after the asset was shown does not move the week either.
With the sector: what they say after the asset was shown moves neither the sector (the day after it) nor the week.
A step is given once to a question, even with room for more: the asset already shown is not planned again at the longer wait.
A chain that names a step twice still gives it once.
With two in a row unanswered a new question gets one follow-up: a fourth unanswered in a row is never handed over.
Once they answer that third one, the week comes.
With the sector: with two in a row unanswered a new question gets the asset and nothing after it.
A chip Bobby wrote starts no chain: tapped after an answered follow-up, about another asset, it is a read Bobby started.
Never two on one local day, even more than 18 hours apart: one shown at two in the morning (the phone was in another time zone) moves the next to the day after.
Never sooner than 18 hours after the last one shown, even on another local day: the hour they answer at would put the week at nine the next morning, so it waits for the Monday after.
Clocks go back (Europe/Madrid, 25 October): the follow-up keeps the hour on the clock, 25 hours after the question.
Clocks go back (Europe/Madrid): a late question the night before still lands at nine in the evening.
Clocks go back (America/New_York, 1 November): the same hour on the clock.
Clocks go forward (Australia/Sydney, 4 October): the same hour on the clock, 23 hours after the question.
A follow-up moved to the next day keeps its hour across a clock change (Australia/Sydney, 4 October): Sunday at 21:00 on the clock, 23 hours after Saturday's.
A question at one in the morning about today, from someone who answers in the evening: the next day at that hour, never that same evening.
A follow-up dated after now has not been shown: it takes nothing from the question.
